outputs.L1: A display element includes a light-emitting unit and a drive circuit configured to drive the light-emitting unit. The drive circuit includes at least a drive transistor and a capacitor. The drive transistor is configured such that a voltage is supplied to one source/drain region, while the other source/drain region is connected to the light-emitting unit, so that a current corresponding to a voltage held by the capacitor flows through the light-emitting unit via the drive transistor. A voltage having a ramp waveform is applied to the other source/drain region in a state in which the voltage of the capacitor is set so that the drive transistor is non-conductive and a gate electrode is electrically floating. A display element is provided with a light-emitting section and a drive circuit for operating that light-emitting section. The drive circuit has at least a drive transistor and a capacitor. In the drive transistor, one source/drain region receives a voltage, while the other source/drain region is coupled to the light-emitting section. As a result, a current determined by the voltage stored in the capacitor is supplied through the drive transistor to the light-emitting section.

In this arrangement, while the capacitor voltage is adjusted so that the drive transistor remains off and the gate electrode is placed in an electrically floating condition, a ramp-shaped voltage waveform is applied to the other source/drain region. Then, with the ramp waveform voltage still being applied, a specified fixed voltage is supplied to the gate electrode. Consequently, the capacitor stores a voltage that corresponds to the slope magnitude of the ramp waveform.
outputs.L3:
A display element includes a light-emitting unit and a drive circuit configured to drive the light-emitting unit. The light-emitting unit may be, for example, an organic electroluminescent element or another current-driven light-emitting device. The drive circuit controls the amount of current supplied to the light-emitting unit, thereby controlling the luminance of the display element.

The drive circuit includes at least a drive transistor and a capacitor. The drive transistor is arranged so as to supply a drive current to the light-emitting unit. The capacitor is connected in such a manner that it can hold a voltage used to control the gate potential of the drive transistor. In operation, the drive transistor supplies current to the light-emitting unit in accordance with the voltage held by the capacitor. As a result, the light emission intensity of the light-emitting unit is determined by the stored voltage.

During a predetermined operation period, a ramp waveform voltage is applied to one source/drain region of the drive transistor. At this time, the voltage held by the capacitor is set so that the drive transistor remains in a non-conductive state. In addition, the gate electrode of the drive transistor is placed in an electrically floating state. Since the drive transistor is non-conductive, current flow through the drive transistor is suppressed while the ramp waveform voltage is being applied.

Thereafter, while the application of the ramp waveform voltage continues, a predetermined constant voltage is applied to the gate electrode of the drive transistor. This operation changes the electrical state of the drive transistor and the capacitor. As a result, the capacitor holds a voltage that corresponds to the slope of the ramp waveform voltage. The voltage stored in the capacitor can then be used as a control voltage for the drive transistor, allowing the drive current supplied to the light-emitting unit to be set in accordance with the ramp waveform characteristics.

Through this configuration and driving method, the display element can generate and store a voltage related to the ramp waveform slope in the capacitor, and can use that stored voltage to control the current supplied by the drive transistor to the light-emitting unit. This enables controlled driving of the light-emitting unit and contributes to stable luminance control of the display element.
outputs.L4:
A display element includes a light-emitting unit and a driving circuit for supplying a controlled drive current to the light-emitting unit. The driving circuit includes a drive transistor, a capacitor, and switching elements arranged so that the voltage stored in the capacitor determines the current supplied by the drive transistor. In operation, a ramp-waveform voltage is applied during a programming period. The gate of the drive transistor is placed in a floating state at a predetermined timing, and the capacitor is charged or discharged according to the slope of the ramp waveform.

As the ramp voltage changes, the floating gate potential follows in a controlled manner, causing the capacitor to store a voltage that corresponds to the ramp-waveform slope and the selected programming condition. After programming is completed, the stored voltage is retained by the capacitor and applied to the drive transistor during a light-emission period. The drive transistor then supplies a current to the light-emitting unit based on the retained voltage.

Because the light-emitting current is determined by the voltage stored in the capacitor, the display element can achieve more accurate current control. This helps reduce variations caused by transistor characteristics, threshold voltage differences, or other circuit inconsistencies. As a result, the light-emitting unit can be driven with improved precision, contributing to stable brightness, enhanced gradation control, and improved overall display performance.
outputs.L5:
A display element is a visual component used to present information on a screen or interface. It can include text, images, icons, buttons, menus, charts, or any other object that helps users understand and interact with digital content. In web design, software development, and user interface design, display elements play an important role in creating clear, attractive, and functional layouts.

A well-designed display element should be easy to see, simple to understand, and consistent with the overall design of the application or website. For example, a button should look clickable, a heading should stand out from normal text, and an image should support the message being communicated. The placement, size, color, and style of each display element can affect how users navigate and respond to the interface.

Display elements are essential for improving user experience. They help organize information, guide attention, and make digital products more intuitive. Whether used in a mobile app, a website, a dashboard, or an electronic device, a display element must combine visual appeal with practical purpose. When designed effectively, it makes information easier to access and interaction more efficient.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style independent claim for an OLED display pixel circuit that uses a drive transistor, storage capacitor, ramp waveform applied to the drain/source node, and then a constant gate voltage to store a slope-dependent voltage.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **An organic light emitting diode (OLED) display pixel circuit comprising:**

a drive transistor having a gate terminal, a first current terminal, and a second current terminal, the drive transistor being configured to control a drive current through an OLED;

a storage capacitor coupled to the gate terminal of the drive transistor and configured to store a control voltage for the drive transistor;

at least one switching transistor configured to selectively couple a ramp waveform signal to one of the first current terminal and the second current terminal of the drive transistor during a programming interval; and

control circuitry configured to, during the programming interval, apply the ramp waveform signal to said one of the first current terminal and the second current terminal of the drive transistor and thereafter apply a substantially constant gate voltage to the gate terminal of the drive transistor,

wherein the storage capacitor stores, in response to the ramp waveform signal and the substantially constant gate voltage, a voltage that is dependent on a slope of the ramp waveform signal, and

wherein the drive transistor is configured, during an emission interval following the programming interval, to generate the drive current through the OLED based at least in part on the voltage stored on the storage capacitor.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into formal patent claim language: a display pixel has an LED, a drive transistor, and a capacitor; current through the LED depends on capacitor voltage; during compensation, the transistor is nonconductive, the gate floats, a ramp waveform is applied to the LED-side terminal, then a constant voltage is applied to the gate while the ramp continues, storing a voltage corresponding to ramp gradient.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A display pixel circuit** comprising:  
   a light-emitting diode having a first terminal and a second terminal;  
   a drive transistor configured to control a current flowing through the light-emitting diode; and  
   a storage capacitor coupled to a gate of the drive transistor,  
   wherein a magnitude of the current flowing through the light-emitting diode is determined at least in part by a voltage stored on the storage capacitor,  
   and wherein the display pixel circuit is configured to perform a compensation operation in which:  
   the drive transistor is placed in a nonconductive state;  
   the gate of the drive transistor is allowed to float;  
   a ramp waveform is applied to a terminal of the light-emitting diode on a side coupled to the drive transistor;  
   subsequently, while the ramp waveform continues to be applied, a constant voltage is applied to the gate of the drive transistor; and  
   a voltage corresponding to a gradient of the ramp waveform is stored on the storage capacitor.

2. **The display pixel circuit of claim 1**, wherein the light-emitting diode comprises an organic light-emitting diode.

3. **The display pixel circuit of claim 1**, wherein the storage capacitor is connected between the gate of the drive transistor and the terminal of the light-emitting diode on the side coupled to the drive transistor.

4. **The display pixel circuit of claim 1**, wherein the ramp waveform is a linearly varying voltage waveform.

5. **The display pixel circuit of claim 1**, wherein the voltage corresponding to the gradient of the ramp waveform compensates for a characteristic variation of the drive transistor.

6. **The display pixel circuit of claim 5**, wherein the characteristic variation comprises a threshold voltage variation of the drive transistor.

7. **The display pixel circuit of claim 1**, wherein the constant voltage applied to the gate of the drive transistor is applied through a switching transistor.

8. **The display pixel circuit of claim 1**, wherein the gate of the drive transistor is floated before application of the constant voltage to the gate.

9. **The display pixel circuit of claim 1**, wherein the drive transistor remains nonconductive during at least a portion of the compensation operation in which the ramp waveform is applied.

10. **The display pixel circuit of claim 1**, wherein the stored voltage is used during an emission period to set the current flowing through the light-emitting diode.

11. **A method of operating a display pixel circuit including a light-emitting diode, a drive transistor, and a storage capacitor, the method comprising:**  
   controlling a current through the light-emitting diode by a voltage stored on the storage capacitor;  
   during a compensation period, turning off the drive transistor such that the drive transistor is nonconductive;  
   floating a gate of the drive transistor;  
   applying a ramp waveform to a terminal of the light-emitting diode coupled to the drive transistor;  
   after the gate has been floated and while continuing to apply the ramp waveform, applying a constant voltage to the gate of the drive transistor; and  
   storing, on the storage capacitor, a voltage corresponding to a gradient of the ramp waveform.

12. **The method of claim 11**, further comprising, after the compensation period, causing the drive transistor to conduct a drive current through the light-emitting diode in accordance with the voltage stored on the storage capacitor.

13. **The method of claim 11**, wherein applying the ramp waveform comprises applying a substantially linear voltage ramp.

14. **The method of claim 11**, wherein storing the voltage corresponding to the gradient of the ramp waveform comprises storing a compensation voltage for compensating a threshold voltage of the drive transistor.

15. **The method of claim 11**, wherein the constant voltage applied to the gate is a reference voltage.

16. **The method of claim 11**, wherein the light-emitting diode is an organic light-emitting diode.

17. **A display apparatus** comprising:  
   a plurality of display pixels arranged in an array, each display pixel including:  
   a light-emitting diode;  
   a drive transistor coupled to the light-emitting diode; and  
   a storage capacitor coupled to a gate of the drive transistor,  
   wherein current through the light-emitting diode is controlled based on a voltage of the storage capacitor; and  
   drive circuitry configured, for each display pixel, to execute a compensation sequence in which the drive transistor is rendered nonconductive, the gate of the drive transistor is floated, a ramp waveform is applied to a terminal of the light-emitting diode coupled to the drive transistor, and thereafter a constant voltage is applied to the gate while the ramp waveform continues, thereby storing on the storage capacitor a voltage corresponding to a gradient of the ramp waveform.

18. **The display apparatus of claim 17**, wherein the drive circuitry comprises a ramp-voltage generator configured to generate the ramp waveform.

19. **The display apparatus of claim 17**, wherein the drive circuitry is configured to apply the compensation sequence before an emission period of the display pixels.

20. **The display apparatus of claim 17**, wherein the voltage stored on the storage capacitor reduces nonuniformity of luminance caused by variations in drive-transistor characteristics among the plurality of display pixels.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Japanese-patent-abstract-style English paragraph describing a display device pixel circuit in which a ramp waveform and floating gate operation are used to set a capacitor voltage that determines current through a light-emitting element.
counterfactuals.output: A display device includes a pixel circuit provided with a light-emitting element, a drive transistor configured to supply a current to the light-emitting element, a capacitor connected to a control node of the drive transistor, and a switching circuit for controlling writing of a data signal. In a setting period, a floating gate node connected to the capacitor is placed in a floating state, and a ramp waveform voltage is supplied to a signal line or a reference line capacitively coupled to the floating gate node. When the ramp waveform reaches a level corresponding to input display data, a sampling switch is controlled so that a voltage corresponding to the reached level is held in the capacitor. The held voltage determines a gate-source voltage of the drive transistor, whereby a drive current flowing through the light-emitting element is set. By using the ramp waveform and the floating gate operation, the pixel circuit can generate an analog current corresponding to the display data while reducing influence of threshold voltage variation of the drive transistor and suppressing deterioration in display uniformity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
